note: The human half of the naming gate. scripts/validate-naming.mjs checks the six mechanical rules; this records a practitioner's judgement on the rule that cannot be mechanised -- whether the name is what someone would say to ask for the operation. Review docs/widget-names.md, which is generated, and record verdicts here. A verdict is pinned to the digest of (nodeType, title, group): change any of the three and the review goes stale rather than carrying over.
ceilingRule: pendingCeiling may be lowered freely and never raised. A widget added after 2026-10-13 has no entry here, which fails the build until one is written, so the pending list can only shrink.

verdicts.accepted: The name is what a practitioner would say to ask for this operation.
verdicts.flagged: Raised in review; carries a note and appears in every build until resolved.
verdicts.pending: Not yet reviewed. Seeded for the widgets that existed when this gate was added.

reviews.title: Aggregate points to H3 cells
reviews.note: Renamed from `hex_aggregate` on 2026-10-19, as the sibling of the above: same operation, different areal unit, and it had the verb after its object with the unit unstated. The unit is the ontology's own term (`fw:HexCell`, "H3 cell") rather than "hexbin", because a plotting library's hexbin is a lattice fitted to its data and these cells come from a fixed global index at a stated resolution. Hexbin is what practitioners say, so it is a glossary pointer to H3 cell and sits in the widget's description, which is what the palette search matches.

reviews.title: Keep points inside the area
reviews.reviewedBy: the practitioner and Claude, in the exchange that asked for it
reviews.note: Named against the rule this ledger states: a transform verb, then what it acts on, with the second operand carried by a preposition -- clip_points_to_area beside summarize_points_to_polygon and snap_to_network. The palette words say the result rather than the operation, "Keep points inside the area", because that is the sentence a practitioner is holding when they look for it; the identifier keeps the discipline's verb.

reviews.title: Evidence register
reviews.note: Purpose supplied by the practitioner 2026-10-19 and recorded in experiment 64, phase 2: built for Gaborone, to check whether facilities from healthsites.io, the Ministry of Health's list and Overture Places were the same facilities. The registry description says what it renders, not what it is for. The name is pending review until that purpose is settled: "Evidence register" names a presentation, and the operation may be source agreement rather than inspection. Manual validation of inputs was scoped out of Fieldwork on 2026-10-19 ("out of scope for FW, for now"), so the activity this widget supports is deliberately not being built toward; its disposition is for the audit queue, not a consequence of that decision.

reviews.title: Summarize points to polygons
reviews.note: Renamed from `summarize_polygons` on 2026-10-19 after the practitioner asked whether it should be "summarize points or summarize polygons". Neither alone: the operation reduces POINTS and the polygons are the areal units it reduces them to, so both operands are named and the second carries a preposition. `summarize_combined_area` is the widget that genuinely summarizes polygons. The mechanical gate recorded no violation for the old name, which is why this ledger exists.

rule: After a transform verb the slot names what the verb acts ON. A second operand is stated with a preposition -- summarize_points_to_polygon, aggregate_points_to_h3_cell, snap_to_network -- never left to the reader and never put in the object slot. A method name stands in for the operation only where the method name IS the practitioner's term, which is the existing exemption that keeps `voronoi`, `isochrone` and `summarize_hull`. Recorded 2026-10-19 with the first two reviews; see docs/audits/ontology-audit.md for the convention it corrects.
